# Compliance and asset provenance

## Assets

**Every asset in this build was generated by code written for it.** There are
no imported models, textures, fonts beyond a Google Fonts stylesheet, sound
files or third-party art.

| Asset | Source |
|---|---|
| Axie models | Procedural three.js geometry, built at runtime from the part list in `src/data/axies.ts` |
| Karts | Procedural, built from `src/data/karts.ts` and the fitted parts |
| Tracks | Generated from route descriptions in `src/data/tracks/` |
| Scenery, hazards, VFX | Procedural, instanced, seeded from the track id |
| Audio | Synthesised at runtime with the Web Audio API — engine, tyres, wind, impacts, music |
| UI type | Inter, via Google Fonts (SIL Open Font Licence) |

Runtime dependency: **three.js** (MIT). Dev dependencies: TypeScript, Vite,
esbuild, ws.

## Axie data

The Axie model in this build follows the real data shape:

- a **class** from the nine Axie classes;
- **six body parts** — eyes, ears, horn, mouth, back, tail — each with its own
  class;
- **HP / Speed / Skill / Morale** recomputed from class base plus +3 per part,
  by the part's class, exactly as the Axie stat model does it. The stats are
  never stored; `resolveAxieStats()` derives them, so a fetched Axie produces
  correct driving numbers with no mapping layer.

**What is real and what is demo data:**

| | |
|---|---|
| The class base stat table | The real one |
| The +3-per-part rule and which stat each class governs | The real one |
| The six part types | The real ones |
| The three drivers' names — Buba, Puffy, Pomodoro | Named for the three models in the official Axie 3D starter toolkit, so the real meshes and rigs drop into the same `AxieDefinition` |
| Their classes, specific parts, colours and bios | **Demo data authored for this build.** Not fetched, not on-chain, and not a claim about any real Axie. |

`AxieDefinition.source` is `'mock-local'` on all three, in the data itself.

## Web3

There is **no chain code in this build**: no wallet connection, no contract
call, no network request to any chain or indexer, no key material, and nothing
that could be mistaken for one.

This is deliberate, and it matches the brief: gameplay before ownership, and a
race must never block on a chain read. The seam where ownership would attach
is documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and is two files wide.

If an integration is later required, the guardrails this build is designed
around are:

- resolve and cache an eligible loadout **before** matchmaking, with an
  explicit timeout and an offline fallback;
- treat chain metadata as an ownership input, never as race authority — the
  server computes race stats from its own rules version;
- use Saigon testnet, never production, for any demonstration;
- keep keys out of source control and out of client logs.

Product naming (Ronin Waypoint is now Ronin Stash) and any SDK choice would be
re-verified against current official documentation at the time of integration
rather than carried over from this document.

## Fairness

- Ranked normalises every loadout toward the kart baseline and caps the stat
  budget, so no purchase is an automatic win.
- Ranked disables assists and sets catch-up to zero. The mode screen says so
  before you choose it.
- Bots have no hidden speed and no dynamic difficulty. A bot is a skill number
  and a personality, and it drives with the same inputs and the same physics a
  player does.
- A result carrying an integrity flag is held back rather than published, both
  offline and on the server.

## Data and privacy

The game stores one profile in `localStorage` under `lunaprix.profile.v3`:
settings, coins, owned parts, rating and records. It is never transmitted. No
analytics, no tracking, no third-party requests at runtime beyond the Google
Fonts stylesheet.

Erasing it is a button in Settings.
